name: Covered Call Roll Up and Out
summary: Management structure, not an opening trade: buy back a threatened short call and sell a higher strike in a later expiry, for a net credit, to keep the shares and raise the cap.

legs.strike_rule: close the existing short call (now 0.60+ delta)
new strike >= old strike, chosen at 0.30 delta in the new cycle
legs.dte_rule: next cycle, 30-45 DTE, at least 14 days beyond the old expiry

max_profit: (new strike - share basis + cumulative credits) x 100
max_loss: full share downside less cumulative credits

greeks.delta: raises net delta back toward +70 per unit
greeks.theta: reset to a fresh positive decay curve

when_to_use: Short call delta >= 0.70, at least 7 DTE remaining, and the system wants to retain the shares (tax, core holding, or the underlying still trending up).
typical_dte: execute at 14-21 DTE on the old leg; new leg at 30-45 DTE
entry_rules: Trigger: short call delta >= 0.70 OR spot > strike x 1.02, with DTE <= 21.
Execute as a single multi-leg roll order (buy-to-close + sell-to-open), never two separate orders.
Require the roll to be a NET CREDIT. If no higher strike in the next cycle pays a credit, roll out at the same strike instead.
Do not roll more than 2 cycles on the same underlying without re-validating the thesis; after 2 rolls, allow the shares to be sold instead.
Do not roll into an expiry containing an earnings date.
management_rules: Cap total rolls at 3 per position; after that, close the unit.
Track cumulative credits as a basis reduction; the unit must remain profitable if called at the new strike.
If the roll can only be done for a debit >= 0.25% of notional, abandon the roll and let the shares go (controlled close).
exit_rules: If the roll order does not fill within 3 attempts at progressively worse prices (mid, mid+5%, mid+10% of spread) before 15:30 ET on expiration day, abandon the roll and simply buy back the short call outright - never enter expiration with the short leg open.
Standard extrinsic guard applies to the old leg until it is closed.
assignment_risk: The window between buying back the old call and the new call being live is the danger zone; a combo roll order eliminates it. If the old call is deep ITM near a dividend, the roll may be too late - close instead.
buying_power: None beyond the shares; the roll is covered throughout if executed as a combo.
liquidity_needs: Both expiries must be liquid; roll spread <= 10% of the net credit.
common_mistakes: Rolling for a debit to 'save' a position; rolling indefinitely and turning a small capped gain into an unlimited commitment; legging the roll and briefly holding a naked call.
zero_dte_notes: Rolling a 0DTE short call is almost always worse than closing it; the new leg's credit rarely compensates for the gamma already realized.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
